method: Re-read 2015 publicly hosted original Phytoneuron PDF, used page screenshots for each Appendix B citation (not only staged crosswalk JSON). All seven species' source records and collector numbers matched the saved provisional cards in GitHub.

Directly read original printed vegetative species accounts for Melica nitens and historical Coelorachis cylindrica and confirmed absent true rhizomes for Melica versus short knotty rhizomes for Coelorachis, with membranous ciliate ligule as source-defined.

Attempted exact voucher search in public web sources and TORCH; no individual barcodes/digitized sheet scans were recovered. Indexed search misses and portal/remote connection failures are not evidence the specimens are lost.

TORCH is an official digitized collection portal for SWT, TEX and LL; available database count and usage rights do not establish any license for a specific sheet unless the exact specimen media record is read.

All source-locality checks are independent of current iNaturalist user labels. They document prior collected specimens, not the correctness of any recent Hays photo and not wild/established status in horticultural species.
County BONAP native atlas is a separate gate not tested this batch; state Texas-native in Kew is not sufficient.
No existing audit/score/gallery/credit/learner files altered; add new evidence memo for coordinator.

records.notes: Source pp.54 and 85 confirms hard, subrhizomatous but not truly rhizomatous crown, 3–6 mm membranous decurrent ligule and a printed Hays gathering. Nodding florets in archive are suggestive; original local sheet never examined.
records.proof: Request image/barcode/complete sheet-label data for Dingee 89 at Texas State (SWT); compare terminal floret, ligule, crown and present-day Hays image.
records.publication: Hagenbuch & Lemke 2015. Grasses of the Texas Hill Country: Vegetative key and descriptions. Phytoneuron 2015-4: 1–93

records.notes: Source pp.42 and 78 names a short knotty rhizome, small ciliate membranous ligule and two Hays TEX-LL sheets under old Coelorachis. Kew regards old name as synonym of Rottboellia campestris; USDA GRIN instead uses Mnesithea cylindrica. Taxonomic concepts remain documented, not merged as extra learner profiles.
records.proof: Locate the two individual Carr/Sanders TEX-LL sheet barcodes or original high-resolution scans via TORCH/PRC; verify grooved/niched flowering axis and pitted sessile fertile glume, then compare archived Hays 684707043.
